newsitem.title: USA: Cohen to give Clinton joint chiefs recommendation.
newsitem.headline: Cohen to give Clinton joint chiefs recommendation.

text.p: Defence Secretary William Cohen is expected to give President Bill Clinton his recommendation for the new chairman of the U.S. Joint Chiefs of Staff on Wednesday, White House spokesman Mike McCurry said.

McCurry, speaking to reporters, declined to say who Cohen would recommend or to confirm reports that Army Gen. Henry Shelton, head of the U.S. military's Special Operations Command, was the front-runner.
Defence officials said on Tuesday that Shelton, a 34-year veteran who was commander of the U.S. military operation in Haiti three years ago, was at the top of Cohen's list.
However, they declined to say if Cohen would recommend him to replace Army Gen. John Shalikashvili, whose term as the top U.S. military officer expires at the end of September.

Cohen's first choice to replace Shalikashvili, Air Force Gen. Joseph Ralston, withdrew from consideration last month after disclosure of an adulterous affair more than 10 years ago. Ralston is vice chairman of the joint chiefs.

McCurry said that Cohen was expected to meet Clinton on Wednesday to make the recommendation, adding that the president was likely to ponder the matter before announcing a decision. He declined to say when a decision might be made public.
